root_cause.text: The SM8450 Qualcomm interconnect driver’s conversion to dynamic IDs left two qcom_icc_node link_nodes entries using old numeric IDs instead of destination node pointers, so icc_link_nodes() dereferenced invalid/NULL destination interconnect pointers at probe time.
root_cause.evidence: The fix changes the two remaining link_nodes entries in drivers/interconnect/qcom/sm8450.c from integer-style IDs `MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG` and `MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC` to node pointers `&qhm_nsp_noc_config` and `&qhm_config_noc`, and the commit explicitly states that “the change to dynamic IDs ... left two links unconverted,” causing a “NULL pointer dereference in icc_link_nodes().”

intent_record.what: The qhs_compute_cfg qcom_icc_node initializer was changed so its link_nodes entry no longer uses MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG and instead points to &qhm_nsp_noc_config.
intent_record.how: At runtime, qhs_compute_cfg will link to a different interconnect node object, causing traffic or topology resolution for this node to use qhm_nsp_noc_config rather than the previous CDSP NoC config target; this corrects the interconnect graph wiring.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `qhs_lpass_cfg` to reference the correct linked interconnect node object for the LPASS configuration path.
intent_record.what: The initializer for `qhs_lpass_cfg.link_nodes` was changed from using `MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC` to using the address of `qhm_config_noc` (`&qhm_config_noc`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, `qhs_lpass_cfg` will now link to the actual interconnect node object `qhm_config_noc` instead of the previous identifier, ensuring the node relationship is represented with the expected target type and allowing interconnect traversal or registration to use the correct linked node.

The root cause is incorrect link_nodes entries still using old numeric IDs instead of valid destination node pointers. This change fixes qhs_lpass_cfg to reference the correct linked interconnect node object, directly addressing that pointer/linking error.

vuln_statements.explanation: This link_nodes initializer kept the old numeric ID after the driver switched to dynamic IDs. As a result, icc_link_nodes() could not resolve a valid destination node pointer for this path and dereferenced an invalid or NULL interconnect node during probe.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs

Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51513bec806fbe1cf9254baed97f115a480bbb53
Author: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:45:37 2025 +0200

    interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs
    
    Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs for
    the interconnect. This gives more flexibility and also allows us to drop
    the .num_links member, saving from possible errors related to it being
    not set or set incorrectly.
    
    Signed-off-by: Dmitry
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it directly shows the converted node initializers and the relevant link representation change from numeric `.links` IDs to pointer-based `.link_nodes` while enabling `.alloc_dyn_id = true` in the descriptors. The root cause is specifically that after converting to dynamic IDs, some `link_nodes` entries still used old numeric IDs instead of destination node pointers. That vulnerable construct is present here: `static struct qcom_icc_node qhs_compute_cfg = { ... .num_links = 1, .link_nodes = { MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG }, };` and `static struct qcom_icc_node qhs_lpass_cfg = { ... .num_links = 1, .link_nodes = { MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC }, };`. These two initializers use bare old-style ID constants in `.link_nodes` rather than node pointers like `&qhm_nsp_noc_config` or `&qhm_config_noc`, unlike the surrounding converted entries which correctly use pointer form such as `.link_nodes = { &qns_a1noc_snoc }`, `.link_nodes = { &qnm_a1noc_cfg }`, etc. Since the descriptors now set `.alloc_dyn_id = true`, `icc_link_nodes()` will interpret `.link_nodes` as destination node pointers, so leaving numeric IDs there matches the stated bug condition and can lead to invalid/NULL dereference at probe time. Therefore the buggy construct is present and the fix is not yet in this commit.

Add driver for the Qualcomm interconnect buses found in SM8
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit fafc114a468ee43b95388bec8a45d042bc3f9344
Author: Vinod Koul <vkoul@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Dec 9 14:18:42 2021 +0530

    interconnect: qcom: Add SM8450 interconnect provider driver
    
    Add driver for the Qualcomm interconnect buses found in SM8450 based
    platforms. The topology consists of several NoCs that are controlled by
    a remote processor that collects the aggregated bandwidth for each
    master-slave pairs.
    
    This is based on the downstream driver by
    Vivek A
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes both the node definitions and the probe logic that consumes their link IDs. The vulnerable construct is present: qnoc_probe() creates ICC links directly from each node's numeric .links entries via `for (j = 0; j < qnodes[i]->num_links; j++) icc_link_create(node, qnodes[i]->links[j]);`. This means any incorrect legacy numeric link ID in a node definition will be used at probe time. The root-cause condition is visible in two node initializers that use old non-SM8450-prefixed IDs instead of the SM8450 dynamic IDs used everywhere else: `qhs_compute_cfg` has `.links = { MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG }` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` has `.links = { MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC }`. In this file, the correct ID style is otherwise `SM8450_MASTER_*` / `SM8450_SLAVE_*`, e.g. `qns_a1_noc_cfg` uses `.links = { SM8450_MASTER_A1NOC_CFG }`. Because these two entries still use legacy numeric IDs, the function will create links to invalid/wrong destinations, matching the described vulnerability. There is no fix present in this commit: the bad link initializers remain unchanged, and qnoc_probe() has no validation or translation to correct them before calling `icc_link_create()`.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51513bec806fbe1cf9254baed97f115a480bbb53
Author: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:45:37 2025 +0200

    interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs
    
    Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs for
    the interconnect. This gives more flexibility and also allows us to drop
    the .num_links member, saving from possible errors related to it being
    not set or set incorrectly.
    
    Signed-off-by: Dmitry
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact node initializers and the conversion from numeric `.links` to pointer-based `.link_nodes`, which is the relevant logic for this vulnerability. Most nodes were converted correctly to destination node pointers such as `.link_nodes = { &qns_a1noc_snoc }` and `.link_nodes = { &qnm_mnoc_cfg }`. However, at least two entries still use old non-pointer identifiers in `.link_nodes`, matching the stated root cause. Specifically, `qhs_compute_cfg` has `.num_links = 1, .link_nodes = { MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG },` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` has `.num_links = 1, .link_nodes = { MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC },`. In a dynamic-ID conversion, `.link_nodes` must contain destination node pointers (e.g. `&some_node`), not legacy numeric IDs/macros. These two initializers therefore leave invalid/NULL destination interconnect pointers for `icc_link_nodes()` to dereference at probe time. Because the vulnerable construct is present and there is no correction in this commit for these entries, this version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
